title: Artwork and synopses from files beside the film
description: Serves "Finding something to watch is easy."; "Their data is theirs.". Poster and fanart images, .nfo files and embedded tags as the only metadata source.
acceptanceCriteria: In Octave (or, until JS-190 and JS-150, the native browser check), a film and a show kept on local disk and on S3 each show their poster, backdrop and synopsis on the home, in Films or Shows, and on the details page; neither store is slower to first poster by more than a measured, recorded margin.
A film with no image and no .nfo beside it shows as it does today, and the scan logs no error for it.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.
notes: Moved into M1's parallel work (#299): a TV home is mostly artwork and titles, and titles that look like file names fail "Finding something to watch is easy." It does not block the cutover. A migration that adds a column to items recreates the shown_items view (SELECT i.* is fixed when it is made; BL-087).
